title: Emrys and the Ghost
premise: Wren Ravensworth, a veteran crash investigator haunted by the death of their family in row twelve of a downed airliner, is pulled into an impossible case when a passenger jet's records vanish mid-flight — scrubbed by a shadowy aviation training network that manufactures disasters to sell its 'solutions.' Teaming up with Emrys, a disgraced air traffic controller who claims the ghost of the vanished flight's captain has been feeding him clues, Wren uncovers that the network's next target flight carries survivors' families, including their own estranged sister. As regulators close ranks and the network's enforcers close in, Wren must choose between legal procedure and burning the whole system down. In the end, they expose the network by hijacking its own data pipeline mid-operation, saving the flight but sacrificing their career — and finally sleeping through the night beside Emrys, who admits the ghost was never real, only his grief wearing a familiar voice.
about_author: Zephyrine Villalobos is a former airline safety analyst who left the industry after a decade of watching reports disappear into corporate archives. They write thrillers from a converted hangar apartment, where the sound of passing planes is both torment and muse.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Opening on the anniversary of the crash, Wren relives the investigation that closed without answers, then receives a call about a new incident: a flight still airborne whose digital footprint has just evaporated. Emotional beat: grief sharpened into professional dread; the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: The Flight That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. At the operations center, Wren confirms the impossible: radar returns exist, paperwork doesn't. The airline disowns the aircraft. A junior analyst whispers about 'the Meridian protocol' before being escorted out. Beat: vertigo — reality itself feels tampered with, mirroring Wren's fractured nights.

chapters.title: Emrys
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Introduced in a dive bar near the control tower, drunk and muttering about a dead captain named Halvard who 'keeps talking.' He contacts Wren with coordinates for where the ghost flight will land. Beat: wary fascination — two broken people recognizing each other's damage.

chapters.title: Contact
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Against protocol, Wren meets Emrys at the coordinates: a decommissioned runway where the vanished plane actually lands, crew unaware anything was wrong. Someone scrubbed them from existence mid-air. Beat: awe curdling into fear as Wren realizes the scale of the operation.

chapters.title: The Training Ground
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Following the crew's debrief trail, Wren and Emrys find Blackwater Aeronautical Institute, a private firm training 'crisis response' — by causing crises. Wren recognizes Blackwater's logo from their family's crash file. Beat: cold fury; the wound gets a name.

chapters.title: Halvard Speaks
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys decodes the captain's 'messages' — cockpit voice fragments he memorized before being fired for reporting anomalies. They point to a pattern: seven flights, seven manufactured disasters, each followed by Blackwater contracts. Beat: belief tested against sanity; love beginning to root in shared purpose.

chapters.title: Paper Ghosts
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren pulls their family's crash file from archive and finds pages replaced with clean forgeries — Blackwater was there five years ago. Their supervisor warns them off, gently, fearfully. Beat: betrayal; the institution Wren served was complicit all along.

chapters.title: The Sister
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Estranged sister Calla, a flight attendant, reveals she's booked on Meridian Air 447 next week — the network's next target, carrying a planeload of victims' families attending a memorial. Beat: guilt and urgency collide; duty to justice becomes personal survival.

chapters.title: Tail Lights
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The pair tails a Blackwater fixer, Ivo Sarn, through the airport underbelly, witnessing him bribe a maintenance chief. They photograph everything — then realize they've been photographed back. Beat: hunter becoming hunted; adrenaline masking tenderness between them.

chapters.title: Safehouse
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Hiding in Emrys's cluttered apartment above a shuttered diner, Wren sleeps for two hours — the first sleep since row twelve. They map the network on butcher paper. Beat: fragile intimacy; found family forming in a room full of ghosts.

chapters.title: The Whistleblower
chapters.summary: Dual POV. They track down the escaped junior analyst, Priya Nair, who confirms Meridian protocol details and names the architect: Director Aurel Voss, once a celebrated safety pioneer. Beat: hope with teeth — a witness, a name, a plan taking shape.

chapters.title: Regulators
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren brings evidence to the aviation authority; within hours it's sealed, Priya disappears, and Wren is suspended for 'unauthorized access.' Beat: despair — justice inside the law is a locked door; the theme crystallizes.

chapters.title: What the Ghost Knew
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys confronts the truth of Halvard: he died exposing Voss years ago, and Emrys's 'haunting' is memory weaponized into purpose. He tells Wren everything, expecting rejection. Beat: vulnerability rewarded — Wren stays, choosing him over certainty.

chapters.title: Sarn's Offer
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Ivo Sarn corners Wren with an offer: walk away, and Calla flies safe. Wren pretends to consider while palming his access badge. Beat: moral tightrope; love against duty made literal in a single held breath.

chapters.title: Breaking In
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Using Sarn's badge, Wren and Emrys infiltrate Blackwater's data center during a storm, racing to copy the Meridian ledger before it migrates offsite. Alarms trip early. Beat: breathless escalation; trust forged under fire.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Inside, Wren finds their own family's crash listed as 'Trial Four' — authored, initialed, celebrated. They nearly break; Emrys anchors them. They escape with partial files as security closes. Beat: rage transmuted into resolve; the darkest knowledge becomes fuel.

chapters.title: Countdown to 447
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Decoding the ledger, they learn Flight 447's sabotage is scheduled mid-flight tomorrow via a maintenance override. Authorities won't act on stolen data. There is one path: get aboard, or get into the tower. Beat: no good options; commitment despite terror.

chapters.title: Boarding Pass
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Calla, told everything, refuses to stand down — instead she smuggles Wren aboard as deadheading crew. Emrys talks his way into the regional tower with Priya, resurfaced and willing. Beat: solidarity; strangers becoming crew, becoming family.

chapters.title: Meridian
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Mid-flight, the override begins — instruments lying in chorus. Wren reaches the avionics bay with Calla covering; Emrys fights the tower's compromised systems to feed true headings. Beat: climax ignition; every skill, scar, and bond converging at altitude.

chapters.title: Burning the Network
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Wren forces the override offline and broadcasts the Meridian ledger to every screen in the tower, the airline, the press. Voss, aboard overseeing his 'demonstration,' is arrested on landing as passengers film. Beat: catharsis — justice seized outside the law, witnessed by everyone.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Hearings, headlines, careers burned — Wren testifies knowing they'll never investigate again, and finds it doesn't hurt. Calla moves in; Priya visits; the diner below reopens. Beat: quiet reckoning; the cost counted and accepted.

chapters.title: Sleeping Through the Night
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Months later, Emrys wakes at dawn to find Wren still asleep beside him — truly asleep. He says goodbye to Halvard aloud, grateful, and lets the ghost rest. Final beat: peace earned, not given; found family holding, love chosen over duty, morning arriving.
